### 2026-11-01: # Making the sensor alive!!! WITH PYTHON!!1!

**2.43h**

# Making the sensor alive!!! WITH PYTHON!!1!

So for this session I decided to write the firmware for my air quality sensor. Since the language I know best is Python, I decided to go with micropython.

I didn't know a thing about micropython, so I had to do some research. I tried watching some YouTube tutorials, but that didn't work because some were too basic and others were too quick for my pace. So, I ended up asking Gemini to give me a micropython crash course considering I had worked with Python for almost a year and can do some decent OOP.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/e6e76e1b64f8772e0abd35ff3aab21fb13cf2c5f6a74926a9d23092c01f70f94.png)

_The crash course_

With that I learned how the Pin class worked, why does micropython need a while loop and where to put my code. Then I decided to setup VS Code to work with micropython because it always complained about the missing machine module, so I installed the micropython_stubs package with pip and configured Pylance:

![Screenshot_20261101_201012](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/059bb4737f0e837c1a31ff36bb6bce64db16ff8b73970e2e931ee43a86e8f82e.png)

Just when I was about to start coding, I got a notification from Slack. Previously, I had sent a message asking other users to give me some feedback on my PCB, and someone had responded! They recommended me to modify my ground pour for aesthetics, which I happily did:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/77ce685340e2664d6f4badb98d34377ff8f7d86187412e75f48267c3f8d2b32c.png)

_The thread_

![Screenshot_20261101_203727](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/fc35bc8909ac96ea14d33ca7cad4c72d96ab4ec6eee1cf857f99ea450ba29f95.png)

_The proof_

After that, I decided to lock in. The first thing I did was figuring out the pin numbers. I thought I had to put the number next to the D labels in the ESP32, but I learned I had to use the GPIO numbers. So I opened my board's manual and started coding.

I also installed an [external library](https://github.com/rubfi/MQ135) for the MQ-135 sensor and the [official micropython library](https://github.com/micropython/micropython-lib/blob/master/micropython/drivers/display/ssd1306/ssd1306.py) for the oled screen (It was mainly downloading and moving files lol)

Then I learned how to read the data from the MQ-135 using the library and how to print to the screen. It was straightforward because there were many examples and written tutorials online. I also used Gemini for rubberducking and some feedback.

After that, I decided to wire up the LED and set up the alarm system. I followed a simple guide on how to do it:

![Screenshot_20261101_211802](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/81c86a39c71dfa69775e026693f22c42ba2080f8333ed0de93c51679ae6c892d.png)

This was pretty straightforward too!

After that, I realized (with the help of Gemini) that my code was stopping the main loop, so guided by Gemini, I learned how to use the time module and time.ticks_diff() to time my logic separately.

Then I added some snooze functionality using my button, again, following an amazing guide:

![Screenshot_20261101_214559](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/ecbe68bab0af5624948500d90e89c131f550245cc05af742becd218f40461f3f.png)

I had a hard time understanding pull up resistors and how 1 was unpressed and 0 was pressed, but I figured it out eventually (lol).

While coding the snooze functionality, I practiced using the time module on my own, and then polished my code using the feedback Gemini gave me (never copy pasting code btw)

And so far, that's everything I did. Approximately 30% of the time was spent learning and debugging (the debugging part was especially hard without a board to test the code on), and you can check the hackatime page to see the time spent coding.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/hld3Z4tOOA3MrvpstF1av8eSaMvDNCLn/a2d6ae036c8f7099d8f675503b2372b85c54b5e9121b0663edb184a02206591a.png)

And that was it! It was an amazing experience and I learned a lot!!!
